catalysts.headline: FDA PDUFA goal date for the ivonescimab BLA (EGFRm NSCLC, post-TKI indication)
catalysts.impact: Binary regulatory catalyst due one day after this research pass's date (2026-11-13); no FDA decision had been reported in sources reviewed as of this pass

catalysts.headline: FDA PDUFA goal action date for the ivonescimab BLA (combination with chemotherapy) in EGFR-mutated, non-squamous NSCLC post-TKI therapy; as of Nov 11, 2026 (3 days prior) no FDA decision has been announced yet in sources found. Filing basis is the Phase III HARMONi trial, which missed its overall-survival endpoint but trended favorably while meeting PFS; FDA indicated a full review with mid-cycle and wrap-up meetings
FDA PDUFA goal action date for the ivonescimab BLA in EGFR-mutated NSCLC — decision pending as of 2026-11-10

Summit Therapeutics reported Q3 2026 results: GAAP net loss $208.4M (-$0.26/share) vs $231.8M (-$0.31/share) in Q3 2025; non-GAAP net loss $160.7M (-$0.20/share); nine-month 2026 GAAP net loss $613.5M vs $860.4M prior-year nine months; GAAP operating expenses $214.6M (down from $234.2M YoY); cash position $629.8M as of 2026-09-30 (pre-dates the AstraZeneca $2B investment, which closed 2026-10-05)

catalysts.headline: Q3 2026 results: GAAP net loss $208.4M (-$0.26/share), non-GAAP net loss $160.7M (-$0.20/share); cash and investments of $629.8M as of Sept 30, 2026; disclosed receipt of $2.0 billion from AstraZeneca tied to an equity investment, and expanded clinical collaborations with AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo
AstraZeneca completes its previously announced $2 billion equity investment in Summit Therapeutics
catalysts.impact: AstraZeneca purchased approx. 108,955 shares of convertible preferred stock, each convertible into 1,000 Summit common shares (i.e., an as-converted basis of ~108.955M common shares)

catalysts.headline: AstraZeneca announced a $2B strategic equity investment via convertible preferred shares (~109,000 shares, each convertible into 1,000 common shares; implied ~$18.35/common-share-equivalent, ~10% premium to recent trading) plus a clinical collaboration on ivonescimab and sonesitatug vedotin, and evaluation of ivonescimab alongside additional AstraZeneca ADCs; announced with updated positive Phase III HARMONi/HARMONi-2 overall-survival data
catalysts.impact: stock +17% after-hours on 9/28 announcement; +19.38% to +21.12% (sources vary) on 9/29

catalysts.headline: AstraZeneca agrees to make a $2.0 billion strategic equity investment in Summit Therapeutics via convertible preferred shares (implied common price $18.36/share), alongside a clinical trial collaboration testing ivonescimab with AstraZeneca's ADC sonesitatug vedotin in several GI cancers, with plans to test ivonescimab with other AstraZeneca ADCs/cancer medicines
catalysts.impact: Secondary trade press reports the resulting stake at roughly 12.0% of outstanding common stock (10.6% fully diluted); Summit agreed to register resale of the underlying common shares with the SEC

catalysts.headline: Q2 2026 results: GAAP net loss $215.7M, EPS -$0.28/-$0.37 (see conflicts); cash position rose to $690.7M including ~$231M raised via ATM facility during the quarter

FDA accepted the Biologics License Application (BLA) for ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy for EGFR-mutated, non-squamous NSCLC after prior third-generation EGFR TKI therapy; FDA set a PDUFA goal action date of 2026-11-14
catalysts.impact: Sets up a binary FDA-decision catalyst; filing is backed by Phase 3 HARMONi data, which met its progression-free survival (PFS) endpoint while overall survival (OS) missed statistical significance but trended favorably

catalysts.headline: FDA accepted the ivonescimab BLA for EGFR-mutated NSCLC, setting the Nov 14, 2026 PDUFA goal date (foundational event for the pending decision above; outside the strict 6-month window but included for context)

FDA accepted the BLA for ivonescimab plus chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated, locally advanced/metastatic non-squamous NSCLC after prior EGFR TKI therapy, based on Phase III HARMONi trial; PDUFA goal date set for 2026-11-14

conflicts: Market cap: ranges from ~$8.7B to ~$12B depending on source/date in 2026; roic.ai's own quarterly series shows $13.56B / $14.71B / $11.56B for three successive quarters, inconsistent with its own live-quote figure of $10.67B.
Shares outstanding: ~793M (roic.ai, 2026-06-30) vs ~797.75M (Equibles, August 2026 snapshot) vs a weighted-average of 778.2M for the quarter ended 2026-06-30.
Cash & short-term investments: ~$691M at 2026-06-30 vs $713M at 2025-12-31 (both roic.ai) vs a conflicting $454.05M figure attributed to Q1 2026 on Fool.com.
Share price: $16.33 close 2026-11-06 vs $17.54 (undated) vs $14.01 close 2026-06-12 — no confirmed figure for 2026-11-13.
notes: Ivonescimab (a PD-1/VEGF bispecific developed by China-based Akeso, which Summit licenses for the US, EU, Japan and other territories) has been approved for marketing in China since May 2024 via Akeso, but remains unapproved in all of Summit's own licensed territories as of 2026-11-13; the FDA PDUFA action date of 2026-11-14 is the single most important near-term catalyst for this name.
